intro_html: This is the pot roast for the first cold week of the year. Apple juice stands in for cider, Dijon and tomato paste keep it from going sweet, and the carrots and potatoes cook in the same liquid until they taste like the roast. It is a full dinner in one vessel with no separate starch to make. Each bowl carries 48 grams of protein and 598 calories for about $5.65 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $5.65 a bowl (at everyday cost), vegetables included, with no rice or noodles to buy on the side. The carrots and potatoes are doing double duty as flavor and as filler.
shop_smart: Plain apple juice does the job of cider for less money and it is on the shelf all year. Skip the seasonal spiced cider, which is sweeter and priced like a treat.
Carrots are the biggest produce line here. The three pound bag almost always beats loose carrots on price per pound, and they keep for weeks in the crisper.
Dijon mustard and tomato paste are both small amounts from containers that last. Freeze leftover tomato paste in spoonfuls so the rest of the can does not rot in the fridge.
Chuck roast, again, on the sale cycle. Every pot roast on this site lives or dies on what you paid for the beef.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt, black pepper, thyme, and Italian seasoning, and sear it in the vegetable oil until browned on all sides.
Move the roast to the slow cooker. Whisk the apple juice, beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste, Dijon mustard, and minced garlic together.
Pour that liquid over the roast, scraping any browned bits from the searing pan in with it.
Cut the carrots and potatoes into large chunks so they survive the full cook, and tuck them around the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef gives with no resistance and the vegetables are soft through.
Lift the roast out, shred it, and return it to the pot with the vegetables.
Taste the liquid. If it reads too sweet, a splash more Dijon or a pinch of salt will square it up.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each of 14 containers, mixing as you go so each one gets beef, carrot, and potato in the same proportion. Each bowl lands at 598 calories with 48 grams of protein.

head.keywords: apple cider pot roast, slow cooker beef, fall pot roast, beef with carrots and potatoes, budget meal prep, chuck roast recipes
steps: Sear the seasoned chuck roast in vegetable oil until browned all over.
Whisk apple juice, beef broth, Worcestershire, tomato paste, Dijon, and garlic and pour it over the roast.
Tuck large chunks of carrot and potato around the roast.
Cook on low 8 hours until the beef and vegetables are tender.
Shred the beef back into the pot and portion into 14 containers.
